components.note: 火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.
艹 (grass, plants) — flowers and growth: 花, 草, 茶; 荣 (from 榮) is a tree 木 in full bloom: flourishing, honor.

example.hanzi: 为国家赢得奥运金牌是一件光荣的事。
example.pinyin: Wèi guójiā yíngdé Àoyùn jīnpái shì yí jiàn guāngróng de shì.
example.english: Winning an Olympic gold medal for one's country is a glorious thing.
example.fact: The ancient Olympic Games, first recorded in 776 BC at Olympia in Greece, didn't award gold medals at all — winners received a simple wreath cut from a sacred olive tree, along with enormous social prestige back home. The modern gold-silver-bronze medal system wasn't introduced until the 1904 St. Louis Games; earlier revivals of the modern Olympics in 1896 and 1900 gave silver medals to first place and bronze to second.

examples.hanzi: 能当上班长,我觉得很光荣。
examples.pinyin: Néng dāngshàng bānzhǎng, wǒ juéde hěn guāngróng.
examples.english: I feel honored to have become the class monitor.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷光荣地退休了,大家为他鼓掌。
examples.pinyin: Yéye guāngróng de tuìxiū le, dàjiā wèi tā gǔzhǎng.
examples.english: Grandpa retired with honor, and everyone applauded him.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 健 is a strong body.
建 (jiàn) sounds exactly like 健; also in 键 jiàn.

example.hanzi: 她每天去健身房锻炼。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān qù jiànshēnfáng duànliàn.
example.english: She works out at the gym every day.
example.fact: 健 means strong and healthy, and it is mostly in compounds: 健康 (health), 健身 (to work out), 健全 (sound, complete), 健谈 (talkative), 保健品 (health supplements).

examples.hanzi: 多运动对身体健康有好处。
examples.pinyin: Duō yùndòng duì shēntǐ jiànkāng yǒu hǎochù.
examples.english: Exercising more is good for your health.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷虽然七十岁了，走路还很矫健。
examples.pinyin: Yéye suīrán qīshí suì le, zǒulù hái hěn jiǎojiàn.
examples.english: Although Grandpa is seventy, he still walks briskly.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
鬼 (ghost) — a creature with a big head and a hollow body. As a radical it brings in spirits: 魂 soul, 魔 demon, 愧 ashamed.

example.hanzi: 妈妈笑着说这个小鬼又调皮了。
example.pinyin: Māma xiào zhe shuō zhège xiǎoguǐ yòu tiáopí le.
example.english: Mom laughed and said this little imp was being mischievous again.
example.fact: The idea of mischievous small demons or imps appears across cultures independently, from European goblins to Japanese oni and West African trickster spirits, and folklorists suggest this may reflect a near-universal way of explaining unexplained mishaps — a spilled bucket of milk or a lost object — before germ theory or simple forgetfulness became the default explanation. Ireland's Halloween tradition of carving turnips, later pumpkins in America, to ward off wandering spirits is one direct descendant of these old imp-warding customs.

examples.hanzi: 你这个小鬼,又在偷吃糖!
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhège xiǎoguǐ, yòu zài tōu chī táng!
examples.english: You little rascal, sneaking sweets again!

examples.hanzi: 小鬼,你今年几岁了?
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoguǐ, nǐ jīnnián jǐ suì le?
examples.english: Hey kid, how old are you this year?

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — giving wealth; also in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
易 (yì) is only a loose sound clue for cì.
予 (yǔ) — to give; as a part it sounds out 预 yù, 野 yě and 序 xù.

example.hanzi: 古代皇帝常常赐予功臣土地和财富。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài huángdì chángcháng cìyǔ gōngchén tǔdì hé cáifù.
example.english: Ancient emperors often granted land and wealth to meritorious officials.
example.fact: In ancient Rome, the patron-client relationship structured much of public life: wealthy patrons granted money, legal protection, or land to clients in exchange for political support and public displays of loyalty each morning at the patron's house, a ritual called the salutatio. Similar exchange systems, such as feudal land grants in medieval Europe or the fief system in Japan, recur throughout history as ways rulers secured loyalty before large bureaucracies or currency economies existed.

examples.hanzi: 愿上天赐予你幸福和健康。
examples.pinyin: Yuàn shàngtiān cìyǔ nǐ xìngfú hé jiànkāng.
examples.english: May heaven grant you happiness and health.

examples.hanzi: 大自然赐予我们丰富的资源。
examples.pinyin: Dàzìrán cìyǔ wǒmen fēngfù de zīyuán.
examples.english: Nature has granted us abundant resources.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — patrolling on the move; also in 道 road, 过 pass.
罗 (luó) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 萝 luó and 锣 luó.
车 (cart, vehicle) — marks wheeled things, as in 转, 轮, 较; 辑 originally meant carriage parts, then gathering and editing.

example.hanzi: 他的推理完全符合逻辑。
example.pinyin: Tā de tuīlǐ wánquán fúhé luóji.
example.english: His reasoning is completely logical.
example.fact: George Boole, a self-taught English mathematician, published 'An Investigation of the Laws of Thought' in 1854, introducing what became known as Boolean algebra — a system reducing logical reasoning to combinations of true and false. Nearly a century later, Claude Shannon realized Boole's algebra could be implemented with electrical switches, laying the theoretical foundation for every digital computer built since.

examples.hanzi: 他说话很有逻辑,让人容易听懂。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà hěn yǒu luóji, ràng rén róngyì tīngdǒng.
examples.english: He speaks with good logic, so he's easy to follow.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事的逻辑有点乱,我看不明白。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi de luóji yǒudiǎn luàn, wǒ kàn bù míngbai.
examples.english: The logic of this story is a bit confused and I can't make sense of it.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and travel, as in 过, 进, 送; 违 is to go against or part from.
韦 (wéi) gives the sound exactly: 违 wéi, also in 围 wéi and 伟 wěi.
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the flesh/body radical (月 in 脸, 脚, 肚); 背 is the back of the body.
北 (běi) — near sound — 背 is bèi; 北 originally pictured two people back to back, which is the sense of 背.

example.hanzi: 他的行为违背了公司的规章制度。
example.pinyin: Tā de xíngwéi wéibèi le gōngsī de guīzhāng zhìdù.
example.english: His behavior violated the company's rules and regulations.
example.fact: In June 1941, Nazi Germany launched Operation Barbarossa against the Soviet Union, violating the Molotov-Ribbentrop non-aggression pact the two countries had signed less than two years earlier in 1939. The surprise invasion, involving over 3 million troops along a front stretching nearly 2,900 kilometers, remains the largest land invasion in military history.

examples.hanzi: 这样做违背了我们的约定。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò wéibèile wǒmen de yuēdìng.
examples.english: Doing it this way goes against our agreement.

examples.hanzi: 他从来不愿违背自己的良心。
examples.pinyin: Tā cónglái bú yuàn wéibèi zìjǐ de liángxīn.
examples.english: He's never willing to go against his conscience.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 挨 is leaning on or being next to, and enduring, as in 挨打.
矣 (yǐ) — loose sound hint (āi vs yǐ); same part in 唉 āi and 埃 āi.

example.hanzi: 他挨着我坐在后排。
example.pinyin: Tā āi zhe wǒ zuò zài hòupái.
example.english: He sat next to me in the back row.
example.fact: 挨 has two readings. āi means "next to" or "in turn": 挨着, 挨家挨户 (door to door), 挨个 (one by one). ái means "to suffer": 挨骂 (to be scolded), 挨饿 (to go hungry), 挨打. Context picks the reading.

examples.hanzi: 书店就挨着我们学校。
examples.pinyin: Shūdiàn jiù āi zhe wǒmen xuéxiào.
examples.english: The bookstore is right next to our school.

examples.hanzi: 请大家挨个儿排队进去。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā āigèr páiduì jìnqù.
examples.english: Everyone please line up and go in one by one.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a guest under your roof; also in 家 home, 客 guest.
兵 (bīng) gives a close sound; 滨 bīn and 摈 bìn share the part.

example.hanzi: 欢迎各位来宾。
example.pinyin: Huānyíng gèwèi láibīn.
example.english: Welcome, all guests.
example.fact: 宾 means guest: 来宾, 外宾 (foreign guest), 嘉宾 (honored guest on a show), 宾馆 (a hotel). In grammar, 宾语 is the object of a sentence, treated as the "guest" of the verb.

examples.hanzi: 酒店里来了很多外宾。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn lǐ lái le hěn duō wàibīn.
examples.english: Many foreign guests came to the hotel.

examples.hanzi: 新郎的家人是今天的主要宾客。
examples.pinyin: Xīnláng de jiārén shì jīntiān de zhǔyào bīnkè.
examples.english: The groom's family are the main guests today.

components.note: 目 (eye) — blinking; also in 看 look, 眼 eye.
舜 (shùn) gives the exact sound.
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.hanzi: 那一瞬间，他终于明白了真相。
example.pinyin: Nà yí shùnjiān, tā zhōngyú míngbái le zhēnxiàng.
example.english: In that instant, he finally understood the truth.
example.fact: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for experiments that generate attosecond pulses of light — each lasting roughly one billionth of a billionth of a second — brief enough to capture the motion of electrons inside atoms, which had previously been too fast to observe directly. To put that in perspective, an attosecond is to one second what one second is to about 31.7 billion years.

examples.hanzi: 就在那一瞬间,灯全灭了。
examples.pinyin: Jiù zài nà yí shùnjiān, dēng quán miè le.
examples.english: In that very instant, all the lights went out.

examples.hanzi: 时间过得真快,一瞬间孩子就长大了。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān guò de zhēn kuài, yí shùnjiān háizi jiù zhǎng dà le.
examples.english: Time flies; in a blink the child has grown up.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.
鬼 (ghost) — a creature with a big head and a hollow body. As a radical it brings in spirits: 魂 soul, 魔 demon, 愧 ashamed.

example.hanzi: 邻居都知道他是个酒鬼。
example.pinyin: Línjū dōu zhīdào tā shì ge jiǔguǐ.
example.english: The neighbors all know he is a drunkard.
example.fact: About a third of people of East Asian descent carry a genetic variant of the ALDH2 enzyme that makes it harder to break down acetaldehyde, a toxic byproduct of alcohol metabolism. This causes the well-known 'Asian flush' — rapid facial reddening, nausea, and a faster heartbeat after drinking — and carriers of this variant who drink heavily anyway face a significantly elevated risk of esophageal cancer.

examples.hanzi: 他是个酒鬼,每天晚上都喝醉。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè jiǔguǐ, měitiān wǎnshang dōu hēzuì.
examples.english: He's a drunkard who gets drunk every night.

examples.hanzi: 别当酒鬼,喝酒对身体不好。
examples.pinyin: Bié dāng jiǔguǐ, hē jiǔ duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
examples.english: Don't become a drunkard; drinking is bad for your health.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.

example.hanzi: 上课的时候要正经一点，别开玩笑。
example.pinyin: Shàngkè de shíhou yào zhèngjīng yìdiǎn, bié kāi wánxiào.
example.english: Be a bit more proper during class, don't joke around.
example.fact: Victorian England produced an enormous market for etiquette manuals, with titles like 'Manners and Rules of Good Society' selling widely from the 1830s onward and dictating everything from how long to leave a calling card to the precise angle of a bow. Modern etiquette researchers note that such formalized codes of propriety often emerge most strongly in societies undergoing rapid social mobility, functioning as a way for the newly wealthy middle class to signal status alongside the old aristocracy.

examples.hanzi: 我们要找个正经的工作,不能总是玩。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zhǎo gè zhèngjing de gōngzuò, bù néng zǒngshì wán.
examples.english: We need to find a proper job and can't just play all the time.

examples.hanzi: 他一脸正经地说:“我不是开玩笑。”
examples.pinyin: Tā yì liǎn zhèngjing de shuō: "Wǒ bú shì kāi wánxiào."
examples.english: He said with a straight face, "I'm not joking."

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 遗 is leaving something behind or losing it.
贵 (valuable) — what is precious is what you regret leaving behind or what is left to heirs.
生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.

example.hanzi: 长城是中国重要的文化遗产。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng shì Zhōngguó zhòngyào de wénhuà yíchǎn.
example.english: The Great Wall is an important cultural heritage of China.
example.fact: UNESCO's World Heritage program was established in 1972 to protect sites of outstanding cultural or natural value, and it now lists more than 1,200 sites across over 160 countries. The Great Wall of China, inscribed in 1987, is not actually a single continuous wall but a network of walls, fortifications, and watchtowers built and rebuilt by different dynasties over roughly 2,000 years, with a total length — including all branches — estimated at more than 21,000 kilometers.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶去世后,给我们留下了一些遗产。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai qùshì hòu, gěi wǒmen liúxiàle yìxiē yíchǎn.
examples.english: After Grandma passed away, she left us some inheritance.

examples.hanzi: 这座古城是世界文化遗产。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔchéng shì shìjiè wénhuà yíchǎn.
examples.english: This ancient city is a World Cultural Heritage site.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
彳 (step, walk) — 彳 is the left-step radical, as in 行, 径, 德; 往 is going toward.
王 (wáng) — near sound — 往 is wǎng, same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这条小路通往山顶的寺庙。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiǎolù tōngwǎng shāndǐng de sìmiào.
example.english: This small path leads to the temple on the mountaintop.
example.fact: The Inca road network, built without the wheel or draft animals, stretched an estimated 40,000 kilometers across the Andes, connecting the empire from present-day Ecuador to Chile. Relay runners called chasquis carried messages along it in a system fast enough to relay news roughly 400 kilometers a day, comparable to modern postal speeds of the era, achieved entirely on foot through some of the world's most mountainous terrain.

examples.hanzi: 这条高速公路通往海边。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo gāosù gōnglù tōngwǎng hǎibiān.
examples.english: This highway leads to the seaside.

examples.hanzi: 哪条路通往火车站?
examples.pinyin: Nǎ tiáo lù tōngwǎng huǒchēzhàn?
examples.english: Which road leads to the train station?

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 他在大学里主修物理专业。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué lǐ zhǔxiū wùlǐ zhuānyè.
example.english: He majored in physics in university.
example.fact: On July 4, 2012, physicists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider announced the discovery of the Higgs boson, the particle responsible for giving other particles mass, confirming a mechanism first proposed by Peter Higgs and others in 1964. Finding it required smashing protons together at nearly the speed of light inside a 27-kilometer circular tunnel and sifting through roughly a quadrillion collisions to spot the extraordinarily rare signature of the particle's decay.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢的科目是物理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de kēmù shì wùlǐ.
examples.english: My favorite subject is physics.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个物理现象,不是魔术。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè wùlǐ xiànxiàng, bú shì móshù.
examples.english: This is a physical phenomenon, not magic.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a ring that encloses; also in 国 country, 围 surround.
卷 (juǎn) gives a close sound; 圈 also reads juàn or juān.
大 (big/man) — the top part, as in 夫. Dictionary story: a big man wrapped in a long cloth, hence 'cover, set'; used in 外套 coat and 手套 glove.
镸 (long) — the bottom part, a long-hair variant of 長. Memory aid: a long cloth over a big person is a coat or cover.

example.hanzi: 他意识到自己掉进了一个圈套。
example.pinyin: Tā yìshi dào zìjǐ diào jìn le yí ge quāntào.
example.english: He realized he had fallen into a trap.
example.fact: The Venus flytrap snaps shut in about one-tenth of a second, one of the fastest movements in the plant kingdom, triggered only when tiny trigger hairs inside the trap are touched twice within roughly 20 seconds — a safeguard that keeps the plant from wasting energy snapping shut on raindrops or debris. Charles Darwin studied the plant extensively and called it 'one of the most wonderful in the world.'

examples.hanzi: 别上当,这是骗子设下的圈套。
examples.pinyin: Bié shàngdàng, zhè shì piànzi shèxià de quāntào.
examples.english: Don't be fooled; this is a trap set by a scammer.

examples.hanzi: 他设了个圈套,想让对方说出真话。
examples.pinyin: Tā shèle gè quāntào, xiǎng ràng duìfāng shuōchū zhēnhuà.
examples.english: He set a trap, hoping to get the other person to tell the truth.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脸 face, 胖 plump, 脂 fat.
巴 (bā) is only a loose sound clue for féi.
白 (white) — the top. 皂 means soap but also black (皂白 = black and white, as in 不分皂白). Memory aid: soap makes things 白 white.
七 (seven) — the bottom, probably a changed older shape. Memory aid only: seven bars of soap. The true origin is unclear.

example.hanzi: 洗手的时候要用肥皂彻底清洁双手。
example.pinyin: Xǐshǒu de shíhou yào yòng féizào chèdǐ qīngjié shuāngshǒu.
example.english: When washing your hands, you should use soap to thoroughly clean them.
example.fact: Archaeologists have found evidence of soap-like substances on Babylonian clay tablets dating to around 2800 BC, made by boiling fats with wood ash. Soap works because its molecules have a water-loving head and a fat-loving tail, letting them surround grease particles and lift them off skin into water that would otherwise never mix with oil — the same chemistry, called an amphiphilic structure, that makes modern detergents effective today.

examples.hanzi: 这块肥皂有一股淡淡的花香。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài féizào yǒu yì gǔ dàndàn de huāxiāng.
examples.english: This bar of soap has a faint floral scent.

examples.hanzi: 浴室里没有肥皂了,我去买一块。
examples.pinyin: Yùshì lǐ méiyǒu féizào le, wǒ qù mǎi yí kuài.
examples.english: There's no soap in the bathroom, so I'll go buy a bar.

meanings: contrary to what one might expect

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person falling over; marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做.
到 (dào) gives the sound: 倒 is dǎo (fall) or dào (upside down).
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 他倒是很喜欢这个主意。
example.pinyin: Tā dàoshi hěn xǐhuan zhè ge zhǔyi.
example.english: He actually quite likes this idea, surprisingly.
example.fact: Velcro was invented in 1941 after Swiss engineer George de Mestral noticed how burdock seed burrs clung to his dog's fur and his own clothing during a walk in the Alps — an accidental observation that led to one of the most widely used fasteners in the world.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜看起来不好吃,味道倒是不错。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài kàn qǐlái bù hǎochī, wèidào dàoshì búcuò.
examples.english: This dish doesn't look appetizing, but it actually tastes good.

examples.hanzi: 你说得倒是轻松,你来试试看。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de dàoshì qīngsōng, nǐ lái shìshi kàn.
examples.english: It's easy for you to say; why don't you try it?

components.note: 车 (cart, simplified 車) — vehicles and transport: 转 turn, 输 transport; compare 轻 light.
交 (jiāo) is close to jiào; also in 校 xiào and 胶 jiāo.

example.hanzi: 这家店的东西比较便宜。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi bǐjiào piányi.
example.english: The things at this shop are relatively cheap.
example.fact: 较 means "to compare" or "relatively." 比较 can be a verb (to compare) or an adverb (fairly). 较真 means taking something too seriously, 计较 is to haggle over small things, and 较量 means to compete.

examples.hanzi: 这两件衣服，我比较喜欢红色的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn yīfu, wǒ bǐjiào xǐhuan hóngsè de.
examples.english: Of these two pieces of clothing, I prefer the red one.

examples.hanzi: 这件事你不用跟他计较。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ búyòng gēn tā jìjiào.
examples.english: You don't need to fuss over this with him.

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 我们应该客观地看待这个问题。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi kèguān de kàndài zhège wèntí.
example.english: We should look at this problem objectively.
example.fact: The checker shadow illusion, created by MIT vision scientist Edward Adelson in 1995, shows two identically colored gray squares that appear to be starkly different shades because of a shadow cast across the checkerboard pattern — a vivid demonstration of how the brain's brightness perception depends heavily on surrounding context.

examples.hanzi: 别人怎么看待我,我并不在乎。
examples.pinyin: Biéren zěnme kàndài wǒ, wǒ bìng bú zàihu.
examples.english: I don't care how others regard me.

examples.hanzi: 父母应该平等地看待每一个孩子。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ yīnggāi píngděng de kàndài měi yí gè háizi.
examples.english: Parents should treat every child equally.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes, as in 阶 steps, 院, 陆; 降 is to go down a slope.
夅 (two feet going down) — shows descent, and gives the sound: 降 jiàng.
亻 (person) — a person bowing low; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
氐 (dī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 底 dǐ and 抵 dǐ.

example.hanzi: 这项新政策有助于降低碳排放。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng xīn zhèngcè yǒuzhù yú jiàngdī tàn páifàng.
example.english: This new policy helps reduce carbon emissions.
example.fact: In 1987, the Montreal Protocol became the first international treaty ratified by every country on Earth, phasing out ozone-depleting chemicals like CFCs; the resulting recovery of the ozone layer is expected to be complete by around 2066, and the treaty is often cited as the most successful environmental agreement in history.

examples.hanzi: 多喝水可以降低感冒的风险。
examples.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ kěyǐ jiàngdī gǎnmào de fēngxiǎn.
examples.english: Drinking more water can lower the risk of catching a cold.

examples.hanzi: 商店为了吸引顾客,降低了价格。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn wèile xīyǐn gùkè, jiàngdīle jiàgé.
examples.english: The shop lowered its prices to attract customers.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 薯 are tubers, as in 花 flower, 草 grass.
署 (shǔ) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 暑 shǔ.
木 (wood, tree) — 条 was a long slender twig, so branch, strip, and then the measure word for long things; 木 as in 树, 板.

example.hanzi: 孩子们最爱吃薯条了。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zuì ài chī shǔtiáo le.
example.english: Kids love french fries the most.
example.fact: The potato was first domesticated by indigenous peoples in the Andes mountains of present-day Peru and Bolivia more than 7,000 years ago, and Spanish conquistadors carried it back to Europe in the 16th century, where it eventually became a staple crop credited with helping fuel population growth across the continent.

examples.hanzi: 我想要一份大薯条和一杯可乐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yào yí fèn dà shǔtiáo hé yì bēi kělè.
examples.english: I'd like a large fries and a cola.

examples.hanzi: 薯条太咸了,我吃不下去。
examples.pinyin: Shǔtiáo tài xián le, wǒ chī bú xiàqù.
examples.english: The fries are too salty; I can't eat them.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.hanzi: 我们在路边等出租车。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài lùbiān děng chūzūchē.
example.english: We waited for a taxi on the roadside.
example.fact: The Roman road network, built up over centuries starting around 312 BC with the Via Appia, eventually spanned more than 400,000 kilometers connecting the empire, and its durable multi-layered construction technique kept some sections in use for more than a thousand years.

examples.hanzi: 路边有一家很小的早餐店。
examples.pinyin: Lùbiān yǒu yì jiā hěn xiǎo de zǎocāndiàn.
examples.english: There's a tiny breakfast shop by the roadside.

examples.hanzi: 别把车停在路边,会被罚款的。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ chē tíng zài lùbiān, huì bèi fákuǎn de.
examples.english: Don't park by the roadside, or you'll get fined.

components.note: 毛 (fur) — marks hair and wool, as in 羽, 毯 itself; 毯 is a woollen rug.
炎 (yán) is a loose hint for tǎn; 谈 tán and 淡 dàn share it.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 晚上很冷,我盖了两条毯子。
example.pinyin: Wǎnshang hěn lěng, wǒ gài le liǎng tiáo tǎnzi.
example.english: It was very cold at night, so I covered myself with two blankets.
example.fact: Merino sheep, originally bred in Spain and later refined into a distinct breed in Australia during the 18th and 19th centuries, produce some of the finest and softest wool in the world, prized for insulating fibers that can be several times thinner than a human hair.

examples.hanzi: 这条毯子又软又暖和。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo tǎnzi yòu ruǎn yòu nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: This blanket is soft and warm.

examples.hanzi: 小孩在沙发上盖着毯子睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái zài shāfā shàng gàizhe tǎnzi shuìzháo le.
examples.english: The child fell asleep on the sofa under a blanket.

components.note: 云 (cloud) — an old picture of swirling cloud; the rain-topped 雲 is the traditional form. Also the old word for say, as in 子曰诗云.

example.hanzi: 天上有很多白云。
example.pinyin: Tiānshàng yǒu hěn duō báiyún.
example.english: There are many white clouds in the sky.
example.fact: Clouds are counted with 朵: 一朵云. Online, 云 has become a tech word: 云计算 (cloud computing), 云端 (the cloud). In classical Chinese 云 meant "to say," as in 人云亦云 (to just parrot what others say).

examples.hanzi: 今天天气好，天上一朵云也没有。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hǎo, tiān shàng yì duǒ yún yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: The weather is nice today, and there is not a single cloud in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 他把照片存到了云盘里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhàopiàn cún dào le yúnpán lǐ.
examples.english: He saved the photos to cloud storage.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 惊 is a startled heart.
京 (jīng) sounds exactly like 惊; also in 鲸 jīng and 景 jǐng.
奇 (qí) is a sound clue for 骑 qí, 寄 jì, 椅 yǐ and 崎 qí; as a word it means strange or remarkable.

example.hanzi: 大家对这个发现感到十分惊奇。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā duì zhège fāxiàn gǎndào shífēn jīngqí.
example.english: Everyone was greatly amazed by this discovery.
example.fact: When archaeologist Howard Carter opened the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun in 1922, he found over 5,000 artifacts virtually undisturbed after more than 3,000 years, including the boy king's iconic solid-gold burial mask — one of the most complete royal tombs ever discovered in the Valley of the Kings.

examples.hanzi: 看到这么多星星,孩子们感到十分惊奇。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào zhème duō xīngxing, háizimen gǎndào shífēn jīngqí.
examples.english: Seeing so many stars, the children were amazed.

examples.hanzi: 他惊奇地发现,盒子里什么都没有。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngqí de fāxiàn, hézi lǐ shénme dōu méiyǒu.
examples.english: He was surprised to find that the box was empty.

components.note: 车 (vehicle) — carrying by cart; also in 轮 wheel, 辆 for cars.
俞 (yú) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 愉 yú and 愈 yù.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 请在这里输入你的密码。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ shūrù nǐ de mìmǎ.
example.english: Please enter your password here.
example.fact: The QWERTY keyboard layout, patented by Christopher Latham Sholes in 1878 for early typewriters, was arranged partly to reduce mechanical jams by separating commonly paired letters — and despite more efficient layouts being proposed since, it remains the dominant standard for keyboards worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用拼音输入中文。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng pīnyīn shūrù Zhōngwén.
examples.english: You can type Chinese using pinyin.

examples.hanzi: 请先输入手机号码,再点击“发送”。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān shūrù shǒujī hàomǎ, zài diǎnjī "fāsòng".
examples.english: Please enter your phone number first, then click "Send".

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.hanzi: 她和前夫依然保持着朋友关系。
example.pinyin: Tā hé qiánfū yīrán bǎochí zhe péngyou guānxi.
example.english: She and her ex-husband still remain friends.
example.fact: Ancient Rome allowed divorce by mutual consent as early as the 3rd century BC, making it markedly more permissive than many societies that followed; a Roman marriage could be legally ended simply by one party declaring intent in front of witnesses, without requiring court approval.

examples.hanzi: 她和前夫是在大学认识的。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé qiánfū shì zài dàxué rènshi de.
examples.english: She and her ex-husband met in college.

examples.hanzi: 前夫每个周末都来看孩子。
examples.pinyin: Qiánfū měi gè zhōumò dōu lái kàn háizi.
examples.english: Her ex-husband comes to see the child every weekend.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 扔 is to throw.
乃 (nǎi) is only a loose sound hint for rēng.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 他把书包扔下就跑出去了。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shūbāo rēngxià jiù pǎo chūqu le.
example.english: He threw down his backpack and ran outside.
example.fact: The discus throw was one of the original events at the ancient Olympic Games in Greece, dating back to at least the 5th century BC, and is famously depicted in the sculpture Discobolus — a bronze original later lost, known today only through Roman marble copies.

examples.hanzi: 他把行李扔下,先去洗了个澡。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xíngli rēngxià, xiān qù xǐle gè zǎo.
examples.english: He dropped his luggage and went to take a shower first.

examples.hanzi: 别把我一个人扔下,等等我!
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ wǒ yí gè rén rēngxià, děngdeng wǒ!
examples.english: Don't leave me behind alone; wait for me!

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 水从这根管子流出来。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ cóng zhè gēn guǎnzi liú chūlái.
example.english: Water flows out from this pipe.
example.fact: The Romans built an extensive network of aqueducts starting around 312 BC, some stretching more than 80 kilometers, using precisely calculated gradients to move water entirely by gravity — the Pont du Gard in France, still standing after nearly 2,000 years, was once part of a 50-kilometer system supplying the city of Nîmes.

examples.hanzi: 他用一根管子给花园浇水。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng yì gēn guǎnzi gěi huāyuán jiāoshuǐ.
examples.english: He waters the garden with a hose.

examples.hanzi: 我想要一根粗一点的管子喝奶茶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yào yì gēn cū yìdiǎn de guǎnzi hē nǎichá.
examples.english: I'd like a thicker straw for drinking milk tea.

meanings: fig. to appear on the scene
used in advertising to mean new product

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — two feet stepping upward: 登 is to climb or board, as in 登山 mountain-climbing.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound hint; 登 dēng also sounds out 灯 dēng and 凳 dèng.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 新一代的电动汽车即将登场。
example.pinyin: Xīn yī dài de diàndòng qìchē jíjiāng dēngchǎng.
example.english: The new generation of electric cars is about to make its debut.
example.fact: The first practical electric car predates the gasoline-powered automobile: inventors in the 1880s and 1890s, including Britain's Thomas Parker, built working electric vehicles, and by 1900 roughly a third of all cars in the United States were electric, before cheap gasoline and mass production shifted the market.

examples.hanzi: 今晚我最喜欢的歌手要登场了。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒ zuì xǐhuan de gēshǒu yào dēngchǎng le.
examples.english: My favorite singer is about to come on stage tonight.

examples.hanzi: 这款新手机明天正式登场。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn xīn shǒujī míngtiān zhèngshì dēngchǎng.
examples.english: This new phone officially debuts tomorrow.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.

example.hanzi: 他的人格深受周围人的尊重。
example.pinyin: Tā de réngé shēn shòu zhōuwéi rén de zūnzhòng.
example.english: His character is deeply respected by those around him.
example.fact: The 'Big Five' personality model — openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism — emerged from decades of statistical analysis of trait-descriptive language starting in the 1980s, and remains one of the most replicated frameworks in psychology for describing how people differ from one another.

examples.hanzi: 每个人的人格都是慢慢形成的。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén de réngé dōu shì mànmàn xíngchéng de.
examples.english: Everyone's character forms gradually.

examples.hanzi: 你不能侮辱别人的人格。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù néng wǔrǔ biéren de réngé.
examples.english: You can't insult other people's dignity.

meanings: to win (a set, a game etc)

components.note: 手 (hand) — the bottom form shows a hand; 拿 is two hands closing 合 on something: to take hold.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 中国队最终拿下了这场比赛的冠军。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó duì zuìzhōng náxià le zhè chǎng bǐsài de guànjūn.
example.english: The Chinese team ultimately won the championship of this match.
example.fact: In 2004, the Boston Red Sox became the first team in Major League Baseball history to win a best-of-seven playoff series after trailing three games to none, coming back to beat the New York Yankees before going on to win the World Series for the first time in 86 years.

examples.hanzi: 他在最后一分钟拿下了关键的一分。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zuìhòu yì fēnzhōng náxiàle guānjiàn de yì fēn.
examples.english: He won the crucial point in the final minute.

examples.hanzi: 我们终于拿下了这个大订单。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú náxiàle zhège dà dìngdān.
examples.english: We finally landed this big order.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — holding something in the mouth; also in 吃 eat, 吞 swallow.
今 (jīn) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 贪 tān and 琴 qín.

example.hanzi: 这个汤里含有很多盐。
example.pinyin: Zhège tāng lǐ hán yǒu hěn duō yán.
example.english: This soup contains a lot of salt.
example.fact: 含 is to hold or contain: 含量 (content), 包含, 含糖 (contains sugar, seen on labels), 含羞 (shy). 含蓄 means subtle or implicit, often used for the Chinese communication style.

examples.hanzi: 这种饮料不含糖。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yǐnliào bù hán táng.
examples.english: This drink does not contain sugar.

examples.hanzi: 她的眼里含着泪水。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnlǐ hán zhe lèishuǐ.
examples.english: Her eyes were brimming with tears.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — blocking with the hand; also in 挡 block, 推 push.
兰 (lán) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 栏 lán and 烂 làn.

example.hanzi: 他在路边拦了一辆出租车。
example.pinyin: Tā zài lùbiān lán le yí liàng chūzūchē.
example.english: He flagged down a taxi at the roadside.
example.fact: 拦 is to put your arm in the way: 拦车 (to flag down a car), 拦住 (to stop), 阻拦 (to obstruct), 拦截 (to intercept). 拦路虎, a "tiger blocking the road," is a metaphor for an obstacle.

examples.hanzi: 警察把我们拦在了路口。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ wǒmen lán zài le lùkǒu.
examples.english: The police stopped us at the intersection.

examples.hanzi: 你别拦着我，让我去说清楚。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié lán zhe wǒ, ràng wǒ qù shuō qīngchu.
examples.english: Don't hold me back, let me go and explain things clearly.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and cords, as in 线 line, 红 red; 绳 is a rope.

example.hanzi: 他用绳子把箱子绑起来。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng shéngzi bǎ xiāngzi bǎng qǐlái.
example.english: He tied the box up with a rope.
example.fact: 绳 is usually 绳子, counted with 根 or 条. 跳绳 (jumping rope) is a common school sport, and 绳之以法 means to bring someone to justice, literally "to bind with the rope of the law."

examples.hanzi: 小朋友们在院子里跳绳。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyǒumen zài yuànzi lǐ tiàoshéng.
examples.english: The kids are jumping rope in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 这根绳子不够长，再找一根吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gēn shéngzi bú gòu cháng, zài zhǎo yì gēn ba.
examples.english: This rope is not long enough, so find another one.

components.note: 车 (cart, simplified 車) — vehicles and transport: 转 turn, 输 transport, 较 compare; 轻 was a light cart.
The right half is a short form of 巠 (jīng), the sound part in 经 jīng, 径 jìng and 茎 jīng — a loose clue for qīng.
车 (cart, simplified 車) — vehicles and transport: 转 turn, 输 transport, 较 compare; 轻 was a light cart.
The right half is a short form of 巠 (jīng), the sound part in 经 jīng, 径 jìng and 茎 jīng — a loose clue for qīng.

example.hanzi: 她轻轻地关上了门。
example.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng de guānshàng le mén.
example.english: She gently closed the door.
example.fact: A whisper typically registers around 20-30 decibels, roughly a million times quieter in sound intensity than a jet engine at close range, which can exceed 140 decibels — the decibel scale is logarithmic, so each 10-decibel increase represents a tenfold jump in sound intensity.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝睡着了,你说话轻轻的。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao shuìzháo le, nǐ shuōhuà qīngqīng de.
examples.english: The baby is asleep, so speak softly.

examples.hanzi: 他轻轻拍了拍我的肩膀。
examples.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng pāile pāi wǒ de jiānbǎng.
examples.english: He gently patted me on the shoulder.

components.note: 用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 这家商店专卖厨房用品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn zhuān mài chúfáng yòngpǐn.
example.english: This shop specializes in kitchen goods.
example.fact: The modern zipper was perfected in 1913 by Swedish-American engineer Gideon Sundback, who redesigned earlier fastening devices into the interlocking-tooth design still used today; it took decades longer, however, before the fashion industry widely adopted zippers in clothing.

examples.hanzi: 这家店卖各种学习用品。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn mài gèzhǒng xuéxí yòngpǐn.
examples.english: This shop sells all kinds of school supplies.

examples.hanzi: 我要去超市买些日常用品。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù chāoshì mǎi xiē rìcháng yòngpǐn.
examples.english: I'm going to the supermarket to buy some daily necessities.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 账 is an account or bill.
长 (zhǎng) hints at the sound: 账 zhàng is close to 胀 zhàng and 帐 zhàng.
单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.hanzi: 服务员把账单送到了桌上。
example.pinyin: Fúwùyuán bǎ zhàngdān sòng dào le zhuō shàng.
example.english: The waiter brought the bill to the table.
example.fact: Double-entry bookkeeping, the accounting method where every transaction is recorded as both a debit and a credit, was first systematically described in 1494 by Italian friar and mathematician Luca Pacioli, earning him the nickname 'the father of accounting' even though merchants in Venice and Genoa had been using informal versions of the practice for over a century.

examples.hanzi: 先生,请问可以买单了吗?账单在哪里?
examples.pinyin: Xiānsheng, qǐngwèn kěyǐ mǎidān le ma? Zhàngdān zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Sir, may I pay now? Where is the bill?

examples.hanzi: 这个月的电话账单比平时高很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè de diànhuà zhàngdān bǐ píngshí gāo hěn duō.
examples.english: This month's phone bill is much higher than usual.

components.note: 異 — the usual explanation is a figure holding something on the head, hence to put on or wear on the head.
纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.

example.hanzi: 戴维每天早上都去公园跑步。
example.pinyin: Dàiwéi měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: David goes jogging in the park every morning.
example.fact: Michelangelo's marble statue of David, carved between 1501 and 1504 from a single block of Carrara marble that other sculptors had abandoned as flawed, stands over 5.17 meters tall and is displayed today in the Galleria dell'Accademia in Florence, Italy.

examples.hanzi: 戴维是我们公司新来的同事。
examples.pinyin: Dàiwéi shì wǒmen gōngsī xīn lái de tóngshì.
examples.english: David is a new colleague at our company.

examples.hanzi: 你认识戴维吗?他是我的邻居。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Dàiwéi ma? Tā shì wǒ de línjū.
examples.english: Do you know David? He's my neighbor.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.
鱼 (fish) — the old 魯 had fish on top; the meaning 'foolish, rash' is later and not about fish. 鲁 is mostly the state and surname Lu.
日 (sun) — at the bottom (from older 白). Memory aid: a fish gaping in the sun is dazed — hence foolish, rash.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在酒吧里弹布鲁斯音乐。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài jiǔbā lǐ tán bùlǔsī yīnyuè.
example.english: He likes to play blues music in the bar.
example.fact: Blues music originated in the Deep South of the United States in the late 19th century, growing out of African American spirituals, work songs, and field hollers, and its distinctive 'blue notes' — pitches bent slightly flat between the standard notes of a Western scale — went on to shape jazz, rock and roll, and much of the popular music that followed.

examples.hanzi: 布鲁斯是一种起源于美国的音乐。
examples.pinyin: Bùlǔsī shì yì zhǒng qǐyuán yú Měiguó de yīnyuè.
examples.english: Blues is a kind of music that originated in the United States.

examples.hanzi: 这首布鲁斯听起来有点忧伤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu bùlǔsī tīng qǐlái yǒudiǎn yōushāng.
examples.english: This blues song sounds a bit sad.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.
夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 别取笑他了,他已经很难过了。
example.pinyin: Bié qǔxiào tā le, tā yǐjīng hěn nánguò le.
example.english: Stop teasing him, he's already very upset.
example.fact: Laughter is remarkably contagious and largely involuntary: research on human vocalizations has found that people are far more likely to laugh in a social setting with others than when alone, even when the content isn't especially funny, suggesting laughter evolved partly as a social bonding signal rather than purely a response to humor.

examples.hanzi: 同学们总是取笑他的发型。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen zǒngshì qǔxiào tā de fàxíng.
examples.english: His classmates are always making fun of his hairstyle.

examples.hanzi: 你不要取笑我,我是认真的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào qǔxiào wǒ, wǒ shì rènzhēn de.
examples.english: Don't tease me; I'm serious.

components.note: 缶 (earthenware jar) — pottery vessels, as in 缸 vat, 缺 lack.
雚 (guàn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 灌 guàn.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 妈妈把糖果放进了一个玻璃罐子里。
example.pinyin: Māma bǎ tángguǒ fàng jìn le yí gè bōli guànzi lǐ.
example.english: Mom put the candy into a glass jar.
example.fact: Glassmaking dates back at least 3,600 years to ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt, but it was the Romans who, around the 1st century BC, developed glassblowing — a technique that made producing hollow vessels like jars and bottles dramatically faster and helped spread glass containers throughout the ancient world.

examples.hanzi: 厨房里有一个装盐的罐子。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ yǒu yí gè zhuāng yán de guànzi.
examples.english: There's a jar for salt in the kitchen.

examples.hanzi: 这个罐子里装满了蜂蜜。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guànzi lǐ zhuāngmǎnle fēngmì.
examples.english: This pot is full of honey.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — the outer box, as in 国 country and 回. The dictionary reading: four walls of a room, with a child (儿) inside; memory aid only, sound-borrowed.
儿 (legs/child) — inside the box, as in 先 and 兄. Memory aid: the shape is simply a box with two legs; it does not explain 'four'.
周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.

example.hanzi: 四周一片寂静,只能听到风声。
example.pinyin: Sìzhōu yī piàn jìjìng, zhǐ néng tīngdào fēngshēng.
example.english: Everything around was silent; only the sound of the wind could be heard.
example.fact: The Orfield Labs anechoic chamber in Minneapolis, certified by Guinness World Records as the quietest place on Earth, absorbs 99.99% of sound and measures background noise at negative 20.6 decibels — so silent that visitors reportedly begin to hear their own heartbeat and blood flow after just a few minutes inside.

examples.hanzi: 我们四周都是高高的大山。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen sìzhōu dōu shì gāogāo de dàshān.
examples.english: All around us are tall mountains.

examples.hanzi: 他环顾四周,没有看到一个人。
examples.pinyin: Tā huángù sìzhōu, méiyǒu kàndào yí gè rén.
examples.english: He looked around and didn't see a single person.

components.note: 王 (jade, 斜玉旁) — precious gems, as in 球 ball, 珠 pearl, 玩 play.
㐱 (zhěn, the right part 人彡) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 诊 zhěn and 疹 zhěn.
贝 (shell, old money) — value and price, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy, 费 fee.

example.hanzi: 这份手稿是极其珍贵的历史文物。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn shǒugǎo shì jíqí zhēnguì de lìshǐ wénwù.
example.english: This manuscript is an extremely precious historical artifact.
example.fact: The Codex Sinaiticus, one of the oldest surviving copies of the Christian Bible, was written in Greek around the 4th century AD and rediscovered in fragments at Saint Catherine's Monastery in the Sinai Desert in the 19th century; its remaining pages are now digitized and split among libraries in the UK, Germany, Russia, and Egypt.

examples.hanzi: 健康比金钱更珍贵。
examples.pinyin: Jiànkāng bǐ jīnqián gèng zhēnguì.
examples.english: Health is more precious than money.

examples.hanzi: 这张老照片对我来说非常珍贵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng lǎo zhàopiàn duì wǒ lái shuō fēicháng zhēnguì.
examples.english: This old photo is very precious to me.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 未经允许,不得进入此区域。
example.pinyin: Wèi jīng yǔnxǔ, bù dé jìnrù cǐ qūyù.
example.english: Without permission, you must not enter this area.
example.fact: Area 51, a highly classified United States Air Force facility in the Nevada desert, was not officially acknowledged by the U.S. government to even exist by that name until a 2013 CIA document declassification confirmed it, decades after it became a fixture of American pop culture and UFO folklore.

examples.hanzi: 图书馆里不得大声说话。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ bùdé dàshēng shuōhuà.
examples.english: You must not talk loudly in the library.

examples.hanzi: 这件事你不得不告诉他。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ bùdébù gàosu tā.
examples.english: You have no choice but to tell him about this.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
皿 (dish) — a bowl-shaped vessel, as in 盘 plate, 盒 box; a helmet is a bowl for the head.
灰 (huī) shares the rhyme -uī; only a loose sound clue.

example.hanzi: 骑摩托车一定要戴头盔。
example.pinyin: Qí mótuōchē yídìng yào dài tóukuī.
example.english: You must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle.
example.fact: Studies by the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration have found that motorcycle helmets are about 37% effective in preventing rider deaths and 41% effective for passengers, and modern helmet standards trace back to designs developed after World War I to protect fighter pilots and dispatch riders from head injuries.

examples.hanzi: 小朋友骑自行车也要戴头盔。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyou qí zìxíngchē yě yào dài tóukuī.
examples.english: Kids should also wear a helmet when riding a bike.

examples.hanzi: 工人们都戴着安全头盔。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen dōu dàizhe ānquán tóukuī.
examples.english: The workers are all wearing safety helmets.

components.note: 车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.
片 (slice, plank) — marks flat pieces and wooden boards; 牌 is a signboard, a card or a tile.
卑 (bēi) hints at the sound: 牌 pái is close to 脾 pí, which shares it.

example.hanzi: 那辆车的车牌号码我记不清了。
example.pinyin: Nà liàng chē de chēpái hàomǎ wǒ jì bù qīng le.
example.english: I can't quite remember that car's license plate number.
example.fact: France introduced the world's first mandatory vehicle registration plates in 1893, requiring car owners to display a name and address plate; the practice spread quickly, and by the early 20th century most industrialized countries had adopted standardized license plate systems to track vehicle ownership.

examples.hanzi: 你记住那辆车的车牌了吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jìzhù nà liàng chē de chēpái le ma?
examples.english: Did you remember that car's license plate?

examples.hanzi: 这个停车场会自动识别车牌。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tíngchēchǎng huì zìdòng shíbié chēpái.
examples.english: This parking lot automatically recognizes license plates.

components.note: 田 here replaces 囟 (skull) in the older form: head over heart
心 (heart) — thinking and feeling, as in 想, 意, 感: 思 is to think over, with head and heart.
纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.

example.hanzi: 学习编程可以锻炼逻辑思维。
example.pinyin: Xuéxí biānchéng kěyǐ duànliàn luójí sīwéi.
example.english: Learning programming can train logical thinking.
example.fact: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman's research, later popularized in his book Thinking, Fast and Slow, described two systems of thought: a fast, intuitive 'System 1' and a slower, more deliberate 'System 2' — a framework that has become foundational in behavioral economics and decision-making research.

examples.hanzi: 我们要培养孩子独立的思维。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào péiyǎng háizi dúlì de sīwéi.
examples.english: We should cultivate independent thinking in children.

examples.hanzi: 他的思维很快,马上就想到了办法。
examples.pinyin: Tā de sīwéi hěn kuài, mǎshàng jiù xiǎngdàole bànfǎ.
examples.english: His mind is quick and he came up with a solution right away.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 带, 帽: 帮 first meant the side of a shoe.
邦 (bāng, nation) gives the exact sound; 邦 itself means state or country.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 他在厨房里是我的好帮手。
example.pinyin: Tā zài chúfáng lǐ shì wǒ de hǎo bāngshou.
example.english: He is my good helper in the kitchen.
example.fact: Guide dogs for the blind undergo roughly six months of specialized training after puppyhood, learning to navigate obstacles and stop at curbs, and even practice what trainers call 'intelligent disobedience' — refusing a command from their handler when it would lead them into danger, such as stepping into oncoming traffic.

examples.hanzi: 搬家的时候,朋友们都来当帮手。
examples.pinyin: Bānjiā de shíhou, péngyoumen dōu lái dāng bāngshǒu.
examples.english: When we moved house, friends all came to help.

examples.hanzi: 我需要一个帮手来整理这些文件。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yí gè bāngshǒu lái zhěnglǐ zhèxiē wénjiàn.
examples.english: I need a helper to organize these documents.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.
立 (stand) — a person standing on the ground line. As a radical it appears in 站 stand, 位 seat, 竟; also in 建立 establish.

example.hanzi: 老师走进教室,同学们都起立问好。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zǒu jìn jiàoshì, tóngxuémen dōu qǐlì wènhǎo.
example.english: When the teacher walked into the classroom, the students all stood up to greet her.
example.fact: Humans are among the few mammals that habitually stand fully upright on two legs, a posture called bipedalism that likely emerged in early hominins at least 4 million years ago; standing upright freed the hands for tool use but also concentrates body weight through the spine and hips in ways that make lower-back problems more common in humans than in most other animals.

examples.hanzi: 升旗的时候,请全体起立。
examples.pinyin: Shēngqí de shíhou, qǐng quántǐ qǐlì.
examples.english: Everyone, please stand up during the flag raising.

examples.hanzi: 听到国歌,大家都起立了。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào guógē, dàjiā dōu qǐlì le.
examples.english: Hearing the national anthem, everyone stood up.
